r: Serial General Purpose Input Output (SGPIO) is a communication method used between a main board and a variety of internal and external hard disk drive bay enclosures. This utility can be used to control LEDs in an enclosure. For more information about SGPIO, please consult the SFF-8485 Specification.

<dl><dt data-o="">-h, --help</dt><dd>displays a short help text</dd><dt data-o="">-V, --version</dt><dd>displays the utility and AHCI SGPIO specification</dd><dt data-o="">-d, --disk</dt><dd>disk name of LED location. Names are sda,sdb,sdc,... Multiple names can be provided in a comma-delimited list.</dd><dt data-o="">-p, --port</dt><dd>SATA port number of LED location, can be used if a disk name is no longer valid. 0,1,2,3,... Multiple ports can be provided in a comma-delimited list.</dd><dt data-o="">-s, --status</dt><dd>status of the LED to set. LED status is: locate, fault, rebuild, off</dd><dt data-o="">-f, --freq</dt><dd>Set the frequency at which the LED should blink (in Hz). Frequency should be an integer between 1 and 10.</dd></dl>

Set the locate LED on SDA with an Intel Intelligent backplane:
sgpio -d sda -s locate
Set the locate LED on SDA to flash at 3 Hz for non-intelligent backplanes:
sgpio -d sda -s locate -f 3
Set SATA port 2 with fault at a 3 Hz flash rate:
sgpio -p 2 -s fault -f 3
Set disks sda through sdf to fault:
sgpio -d sda,sdb,sdc,sdd,sde,sdf -s fault
sgpio should return zero when successful. It will return with a non-zero value if there was a failure.
